title: Hallo!

learn.heading: Greetings: formal and informal
learn.text: German has two ways of saying "you": **du** (informal: friends, family, students, colleagues in many companies) and **Sie** (formal: strangers, offices, doctors, shops). When in doubt, start with **Sie**. Greetings depend on the time of day. In the south (Bavaria) you also hear **Servus** and **Grüß Gott**; in Aachen and the west, **Moin** and **Tach** are common.

examples.de: Auf Wiedersehen und einen schönen Tag!
examples.en: Goodbye and have a nice day!

learn.heading: Introducing yourself
learn.text: Use **Ich heiße …** or **Mein Name ist …** to give your name. Ask with **Wie heißen Sie?** (formal) or **Wie heißt du?** (informal). After you hear a name, say **Freut mich!** (nice to meet you). If you did not understand something, say **Wie bitte?** or **Können Sie das bitte wiederholen?** Nobody minds, and it is the best way to practise.

examples.de: Ich heiße Ahmed. Und wie heißen Sie?
examples.en: My name is Ahmed. And what is your name?
Nice to meet you, Mr Schmidt.

learn.heading: The alphabet and key sounds
learn.text: German is written the way it is spoken, so learn a few sound rules and you can read almost anything. The letters **ä, ö, ü** are real letters, and **ß** (Eszett) is a sharp *s* after long vowels. Spell your name on the phone like this: A-H-M-E-D (ah · heh · em · eh · deh). The most important sounds are in the table.

tip: Say the greeting that fits the clock: Morgen until about 11, Tag during the day, Abend from about 6 pm. Greet shopkeepers and neighbours first: in Germany a short "Guten Tag" when you walk into a Bäcker or a waiting room is normal and polite.

exercises.q: You enter a doctor's office at 10 am. What do you say?
exercises.explain: Gute Nacht is only for going to bed. At the doctor's use a formal greeting: Guten Morgen.
dir belongs to du. Ihnen and Sie are formal.

exercises.q: How do you pronounce the ie in "Dienstag"?
exercises.explain: ie is always a long ee sound; ei is the "eye" sound.

exercises.q: A stranger speaks fast and you did not understand. What do you say?
exercises.explain: Wie bitte? means "pardon?" and asks the person to repeat.
Until about 11 am you say Guten Morgen.
The formal question is Wie geht es Ihnen? Informal: Wie geht's dir?
Male people are masculine: der Herr.
Female people are feminine: die Frau.
These five phrases carry you through every shop and office.
In a statement the verb is in position 2: Ich (1) heiße (2) Ali.
A question word comes first, then the verb: Wie heißen Sie?

exercises.en: Good evening, nice to meet you.
exercises.explain: Guten Abend is the evening greeting; Freut mich is the standard reply when you meet someone.
Yes/no question: verb first. Formal: Sprechen Sie …? Informal: Sprichst du …?
